extracted.intended_audience: experimental physicists / metrologists performing precision pendulum experiments
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and observational/reporting standards for measuring the vibrations of an invariable pendulum under varying atmospheric conditions (air, rarefied gas, hydrogen) and for deriving the reduction to a vacuum. Includes instrument handling, corrections, and meteorological record-keeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vibration counting and series reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the number of vibrations per diem for each observation series (commencing series, concluding series, and means). Report series-specific values and overall means for comparisons and further deductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the clock correction (e.g., 'Clock gaining 4m 14s.38'), indicate which series are being compared (commencing/concluding), and present the mean values used in later deductions (e.g., vibrations in hydrogen, in air, and in vacuum derived values).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperature measurement and reduction to standard temperature
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure included and external thermometer temperatures during each series and apply reductions to standardized temperatures (reductions to 36° and to 32° Fahr. are used throughout).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report thermometer readings for numbered thermometers (e.g., 35, 36, 37...), give mean temperatures for series, apply 'Reduction to 36°' or 'Reduction to 32°' as appropriate, and state any index corrections applied (e.g., 'Index +0.32').

rubrics_metrics.name: Barometer reading, capillarity correction, and reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure barometric pressure and apply capillarity correction and reduction to the standard temperature (32° Fahr.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report barometer readings alongside the capillarity correction (e.g., 'Capill. + 0.019; Reduction to 32° — 0.012; = 30.342'), indicate the standard barometer value used, and include gauge readings where the interior pressure is measured (e.g., gauge 0.872 inch).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arc measurement and correction for arc
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the arc (registered and true arc) for pendulum swings and apply a correction for arc when computing corrected vibrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide columns for 'Arc registered and true Arc', 'Correction for Arc', 'Reduction to 36°', and 'Corrected Vibrations at 36°'. Use disappearance/reappearance/coincidence timing to derive arc-related corrections ('Disapp.', 'Re-app.', 'Coincidence').

rubrics_metrics.name: Disappearance / reappearance / coincidence timing and interval computation
rubrics_metrics.description: Record times of disappearance, reappearance, and coincidences to compute mean intervals and derive Divisions/interval statistics used in vibration calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report raw times (h m s), compute mean intervals and Div. o values (e.g., 'Div. o 0.96 = 1.15'), and carry these through to corrected vibration values. Provide per-series Div. and associated computed quantities (e.g., '+ 1.11', '+ 1.60' adjustments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Atmosphere control: selection, introduction and pressure equilibration of gases
rubrics_metrics.description: Control the atmosphere inside the apparatus (ordinary air, hydrogen gas, rarefied hydrogen) by evacuating/introducing gases to specified gauge/barometer values and establishing pressure equilibrium before observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe stepwise procedure: withdraw air to a specified gauge (e.g., 0.7 inch), introduce hydrogen passed through drying cylinder until internal barometer approximates external, then pump out to target gauge (e.g., 1.4 inch), allow small escape to produce equilibrium, and record the included barometer (e.g., 'The mercury in the included barometer stood at 29.95').

rubrics_metrics.name: Gas purification and drying procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure introduced gases are dried/purified (e.g., passing hydrogen through a cylinder containing muriate of lime) prior to filling the apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include drying agent in the transfer line between gasometer and apparatus, repeat filling if necessary with fresh muriate of lime, and record who performed the operation and any handling notes (e.g., 'gas was obtained under Mr. Newman’s superintendence' and 'cylinder containing fresh muriate of lime').

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of gas purity by independent analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify the purity of the gas used (e.g., send a bottled sample for chemical/analytical examination) and report the finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the recipient of the examination, the result (e.g., 'no appreciable quantity of air... less than 1/100th part'), and note the expected negligible effect on experiments when impurity is below stated threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and reporting of gauges for residual pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure and report residual pressure/gauge readings when rarefying gas or evacuating (e.g., gauge indicated 0.7 inch, 0.8 inch, 0.872 inch) and relate gauge values to internal barometer and vibration results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State gauge values explicitly with associated observations and compute differences in vibrations corresponding to changes in gauge (e.g., 'pendulum made 1.95 vibration per diem more when gauge reduced to 0.872 inch').

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeatability: replicate observations across days/conditions and average
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeat series of observations (different days, multiple impulses) and compute means to assess reproducibility of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present individual series, report commencing and concluding series, then compute means; compare repeated experiments (e.g., Exp. VII and VIII) and show corroboration (similar results on repetition). Report small differences and average them (e.g., derive mean excess/defect within glasses across multiple experiments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Observer identification and use of independent observers
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the observers for each series (e.g., 'Captain Sabine', 'Mr. Taylor') and attribute observation series to named observers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List observer names alongside each series so that repeatability and observer-dependent biases can be evaluated; include number of coincidences and any observer-specific notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus condition checks and maintenance logging
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine and report the physical condition of apparatus components (knife edge, agate planes, screws) before/after experiments to ensure no mechanical changes affected results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state checks and findings (e.g., 'knife edge being examined, was found apparently as clean and sharp as when first used; agate planes had retained their horizontality; screws were as tight'). Record any adjustments made or lack thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of enclosure effects (glasses removed/replaced)
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether the presence of enclosing glasses affects pendulum vibrations by removing and replacing glasses in successive observations with free communication to external air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower foot screws to detach upper glass, remove/replace glasses between observations, maintain the apparatus otherwise identical, and record vibrations in free air vs within glasses to quantify effect (report excess/defect values and mean).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of reduction to vacuum and retardation values
rubrics_metrics.description: Derive the 'reduction to a vacuum' value for the pendulum by combining measured vibrations under different atmospheres and computing differences (retardation) attributable to the presence of gas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measured vibrations in hydrogen/air and combine to compute vacuum value (e.g., 'number of vibrations per diem of the pendulum in a vacuum derived from vibrations in hydrogen gas is 86316.95'), compute reduction to vacuum for given barometer/temperature conditions (e.g., 2 vibrations per diem for hydrogen at 40° under 30 inches), and report retardation differences (e.g., 10.56 vibrations per diem for air).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison of retardations between gases and physical interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare retardations induced by different gases (air vs hydrogen) and interpret the ratio relative to densities, considering additional fluid properties (e.g., viscidity) if experimental ratio differs from density ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute ratio of retardations (e.g., ~10.55:2 or ~10.41:2), compare to expected ratio from densities (~13:1), discuss whether discrepancy suggests an inherent resistance property of elastic fluids analogous to viscidity, and recommend further experiments with other gases and improved apparatus if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index corrections and instrument calibration notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply index corrections and any instrument calibration offsets when computing corrected barometer/temperature values (e.g., 'Index +0.32').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state index values and their effect on reductions (e.g., '29.875; Index +0.32; Reduction to 32° — 0.025; = 30.17'), and include these calibrations in reported corrected results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise tabulation and reporting format for observational data
rubrics_metrics.description: Present observational data in tabular form with columns for thermometers, included barometer, times of disappearance/reappearance/coincidence, mean intervals, Div. o, corrections, reductions, and corrected vibrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use systematic tables with labelled columns (Observer, Thermometers, Included Barom., Times of Arc registered and true Arc, Mean Interval, Correction for Arc, Reduction to 36°, Corrected Vibrations at 36°) to allow reproducibility and independent verification. Include units (inch, h m s, degrees Fahr., vibrations per diem).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meteorological journal standards and daily observanda
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a meteorological journal accompanying experiments, recording 9 A.M./3 P.M. readings, dew point, external thermometer, barometer, rain (read off at 9 A.M.), wind direction, and remarks on weather; compute monthly means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include per-day entries for barometer (corrected for capillarity and reduced to 32°), external thermometer (Fahrenheit), dew point, rain amounts and wind direction, and summary monthly means (e.g., 'Monthly Mean of the Barometer, corrected for Capillarity and reduced to 32° Fahr.'). Also log heights of instruments (cistern, rain gauge) and observation times (Mean Time).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record instrument placement and local observanda metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Document heights and placements of instruments and other observational metadata that affect readings (e.g., 'Height of the Cistern... = 83 feet 2½ in.', 'External Thermometer is 2 feet higher than the Barometer cistern').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State heights above fixed marks and mean sea level, receiver heights, which thermometer is external vs included, and the conventions used (hours of observation are Mean Time, thermometers graduated in Fahrenheit, barometer divisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Propagation of small differences and reporting of small effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Report small measured differences (fractions of a vibration per diem, small Div. o changes, tenths of an inch in gauge/barometer) and aggregate them statistically (e.g., mean excess/defect across experiments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show per-experiment small differences (e.g., 'the vibrations within the glasses are in defect 0.15 per diem'), combine multiple experiments to get mean effects (e.g., mean defect 0.007 per diem), and discuss their significance relative to experimental precision.
